summary: curve-underlying cannot be ported faithfully to declarative Swap JSON on the pinned 104ff465 framework. The decisive gap is per-direction value settlement: the native-alias variant derives directOutput per route from underlyingNativeAssets(direction) plus the independently proven direction.recipient flag (execution.ts:22-30), while declarative execution has one static settlement.directOutput boolean per variant (declarative-execution.ts:17-20,355; declarative-family.ts:165-166) and selects the variant only by descriptor (declarative-family.ts:240-247). A static true over-claims direct-output for native-alias ERC20-output directions whose receiver overload was not proven; a static false drops the verified native-output direct path (and native-output direct is not even advertised without quoteOutput.nativeBoundary, declarative-execution.ts:1016-1018); a contextChecks rejection throws instead of returning the family's null fallback (declarative-execution.ts:1026-1035). The family's own production test asserts both sides in one run (native-alias-contract.ts:1043-1067), so no boolean value can pass. A per-descriptor split cannot fix this because both proven and unproven directions share one instance/descriptor. Secondary gaps make the other lineages equally unsafe to claim: pricing.refreshPolicy is a per-variant enum (pricing.ts:45-50 vs declarative-family.ts:148-149,163) while the metaregistry lineage mixes on-touch plain pools with each-block classic-meta/legacy-plain pools, and splitting that lineage would compile and run a duplicate multi-stage identity per variant (declarative-family.ts:353-365, adapter-family-runtime.ts:3604-3612,3764-3780). No canonical JSON was authored and the handwritten production entry remains authoritative; narrowing the family or over-claiming settlement would be required.

decisiveBlocker.capability: direct-output raw-receiver settlement is per route/direction: native-alias pools support direct output when the output is native (to the executor) or when the direction's receiver overload was independently execution-proven; classic-meta pools support direct output per bound implementation; plain/legacy-plain/lending have no direct output

existingSource.fact: buildRuntimeLeg computes directOutput as d.nativeAlias ? assets?.output === 'native' || direction?.recipient === true : !d.lending && !d.legacyPlain && supportsClassicUnderlyingRecipient(d.quoteModel), and returns null for a direct-output request when that per-route value is false.

underlyingNativeAssets maps one direction's i/j to input/output native vs ERC20; the native alias program rejects an external recipient for native output (nativeOut requires recipient == actor) while allowing it for ERC20 output.
Identity issues a separate recipient-execution probe only for non-native outputs and records recipient:true per direction; facts.verifiedDirections carries that flag into the descriptor.

The receiver overload is proven by a dedicated executor-program simulation against UNDERLYING_PROBE_RECEIVER and decoded per direction; native output is explicitly excluded ('raw native output belongs to executor').

Production test asserts the passed (recipient-proven) instance builds direct legs with settlement.directOutput=true for every route, while the baseline (unproven) instance builds a direct leg only where route.executionAssets.output === 'native'. Both cases run in one test for the same family. No static directOutput value can satisfy the unproven ERC20-output route and the proven/native-output route at the same time.
Classic-meta contract test expects a direct leg with settlement {directOutput:true} and a null deferred-input leg for every one of its twelve directions.

frameworkLimitation.fact: SharedConversionExecution.settlement.directOutput is a single boolean; compile/validation reject any non-boolean non-static value.
Each variant requires settlement.directOutput to be a boolean at registration.

Variant selection is per descriptor (match expression) and each declarative variant compiles its own identity; there is no per-route/per-direction variant or shared identity. Two variants cannot split the directions of one descriptor.

supportsDeclarativeSettlement for direct-output checks only the static directOutput boolean, quote-asset support, and (for native output) recipient == executor; it never consults a descriptor direction flag such as verifiedDirections[].recipient.

declarativeSettlementCapabilities advertises directOutput only when the static boolean is true and, for native output, quoteOutput.nativeBoundary === true. The family's native-output direct path has no quoteOutput module, so a JSON variant would not advertise that verified capability without adding a quote program that changes the execution call set.

buildDeclarativeRuntimeLeg returns null only when the static settlement support check fails; once a direct-output request is accepted it always builds. There is no declared per-route predicate that can return the family's null fallback for an unproven direction.

probe.method: Temporary tsx probe (listener/tmp-cu-direct-probe.mts, removed) built one synthetic native-alias descriptor with three directions (WETH->USDC unproven, USDC->WETH native output, DAI->USDC recipient-proven), projected the real family routes, and compared curveUnderlyingExecution.buildRuntimeLeg against supportsDeclarativeSettlement/declarativeSettlementCapabilities for one static directOutput=true execution declaration.
probe.consequence: Static true over-claims the unproven WETH->USDC direction (accepted and advertised instead of the family's null) and still fails to advertise the family's native-output direct capability; static false would reject the proven directions. This reproduces the production test's contradictory expectations at native-alias-contract.ts:1056-1059.

decisiveBlocker.whyPartialCutoverIsNotAcceptable: Choosing static true routes output/recipient authority for directions that were never proven and changes the central null fallback into a real leg; choosing static false drops the verified native-output and receiver-proved direct paths (a settlement capability loss). Rejecting at execution time throws instead of returning null. Splitting the native-alias descriptor into multiple variants cannot help because the mixed directions live in one instance and variant selection is descriptor-level. There is no JSON-only way to state the family's per-direction direct capability.

additionalBlockers.capability: each-block vs on-touch pricing is per descriptor, not per lineage

existingSource.fact: refreshPolicyForInstance returns each-block for nativeAlias/quoteModel/lending and on-touch otherwise.
Contract test asserts each-block for quoteModel and on-touch for the same descriptor with quoteModel removed.

frameworkLimitation.fact: pricing.refreshPolicy is a closed enum literal per variant and refreshPolicyForInstance returns select(descriptor).document.pricing.refreshPolicy; it cannot read a descriptor field such as quoteModel/legacyPlain.

additionalBlockers.consequence: The metaregistry variant must choose each-block (over-refresh every plain pool) or on-touch (miss A/meta-rate ramp updates for classic-meta/legacy-plain pools). Either is a behavior change and one side is a pricing-correctness gap.

additionalBlockers.capability: splitting the metaregistry lineage by refresh/direct-output without duplicating the full staged identity

existingSource.fact: The metaregistry identity variant is one staged workflow with registry-surface reads, a per-direction behavior probe, optional scale probing and one final evidence hash; classic-meta and legacy-plain bindings are derived inside the same decode.

frameworkLimitation.fact: Only the primary variant may reuse document.identity.definition; every child variant compiles its own identity from its own abi/constants/expressions/programs/identity.

All applicable identity variants run independently and are merged only by identity key; a duplicated metaregistry identity would run the full probe per candidate and produce extra evidence/provenance work.

additionalBlockers.consequence: Splitting the metaregistry lineage by quoteModel/legacyPlain/plain to fix refresh or directOutput would require 2-3 copies of the same multi-stage identity; candidate cost and identity evidence would change, and the extra variants would alter the declared identity-variant ledger. This is not a faithful 1:1 encoding.

additionalBlockers.capability: four mutation groups with distinct address sets/accept predicates (pool logs, base LP, base pool calls, legacy controls)

existingSource.fact: compileAddressMutations builds separate logs/lp/calls/controls groups with different addresses and accept predicates, then unions affected keys.

frameworkLimitation.fact: Each variant declares one mutationAddresses expression, one optional mutationPredicate, and the root mutationKinds list; compileAddressMutations receives a single group per state key.

additionalBlockers.consequence: A single union address list and predicate would over-refresh (e.g. USDT control logs on non-base pools, LP Transfers on every route) or drop the base-LP/USDT-control/legacy-control filtering. Affected state-key targeting is not equal.

additionalBlockers.capability: retained-channel reverse binding by implementation code plus registry/factory/lending topology

existingSource.fact: The custom reverse binding re-reads code/storage/calls to prove MetaRegistry, legacy-factory, V1 or lending membership before nominating an address surface.

frameworkLimitation.fact: The mapped discovery format accepts only reverseBinding:'address-surface'; custom implementation reverse binding is not declarable.

additionalBlockers.consequence: A JSON port would nominate address surfaces by fingerprint only and lose the registry/factory/lending pre-filter; identity would still reject non-members, but retained-channel nomination work and observation volume change.

additionalBlockers.capability: current pricing stops after the first positive amount among candidate amounts and only queries later candidates when all earlier ones are zero

existingSource.fact: buildDependentProgram emits candidate[0] first, then returns null when firstPositiveQuote is positive; otherwise emits the remaining candidates.

frameworkLimitation.fact: Read-flow step `when` is evaluated before any evidence of that invocation and all active steps run; there is no result-dependent early stop or null-return from a dependent round.

additionalBlockers.consequence: JSON would have to run every candidate quote for every pricing round (extra reads/latency) or pick a fixed candidate (different amount/quote behavior). It cannot reproduce the family's stop-after-first-positive schedule.

nonBlockingAnalysis.note: The above gaps are about faithful declaration, not about the prices/execution being impossible to calculate.
expressibleWithJsonPlusFamilyMath: Registry-surface identity, behaviour probes over i/j and CURVE_BEHAVIOR_PROBE_AMOUNTS, verifiedDirections projection, and route projections can be written as JSON expressions plus registered family math.

Classic-meta binding/guard/quote math (code hashes, slots, 4096-byte forwarder normalization, base-pool mint/exchange) and legacy-plain invariant/fee math can be moved into family math models because JSON `model` calls may return arbitrary bigint/object results.

Native-alias execution/approval/native-boundary steps and lending raw effect-delta-simulation preCalls can be declared directly as AdapterRequest data; the declarative pseudo-request bridge is not the only possible request form.
Discovery events/calls, poolMaterialization and receiptEvent match/impact projections can express the swap observation; source-bound receiptReads (eth-call only) could re-read registry coins.
deviationsStillToReviewIfUnblocked: Identity provenance/evidence hash will differ if the workflow or merge order changes; existing Ready/memo entries need selective revalidation.

routeKey can be declared with routes.key to match the legacy \u001f-joined key, but bindingRef.fingerprint must reproduce curveUnderlyingStaticBindingProjection including recipient flags and variant projections; otherwise Ready/graph keys change.
The declarative route still injects target/direction/adapterId and hashes the full projected route, so any consumer that compares a handwritten route object by hash must be revalidated.

Receipt observation uses descriptor/source reads rather than the handwritten resolveBinding re-reads unless receiptReads is added; factory/lending control reads and error semantics need a separate review.
Exact/quote read-flow rounds cannot stop after the first positive candidate; latency and read counts need a timing review even if amounts match.
